p-356.example: Ordinary soles on ice have a static friction coefficient near 0.1, so they slip at only about 5.7° (⁻¹0.1), while crampon points can hold on far steeper ice.
p-356.actionItem: Before your hike today, check that your crampon points are not dull and the straps tighten firmly.

p-357.title: Choose laser pointers rated 1mW or less
p-357.summary: An eye-safe laser pointer is a Class 2 unit of 1mW or less. Higher power cannot be fully blocked even by the blink reflex.
p-357.principle: The blink reflex takes about 0.25 s and energy into the eye is E=P t. The smaller the beam cross-section, the larger the irradiance I=P/A.
p-357.example: 1mW for 0.25 s is E=0.25 mJ. A 3mm beam has I=1mW/7.1 × 10⁻⁶ m² ≈ 140W/m². Cheap pointers sometimes exceed their labeled power.
p-357.actionItem: Today, check your laser pointer for a Class 2, 1mW or less label, and never aim it at people, animals or vehicles.

p-358.title: Wood and briquette stoves burn better with a taller chimney
p-358.summary: A taller chimney with hotter gas inside pulls harder (draft), so the fire lights well and smoke clears.
p-358.principle: By the chimney effect, draft pressure is ΔP=gh(ρ_out-ρ_in), proportional to height h and the density difference.
p-358.example: With a 5m chimney, 0°C outside air (1.29kg/m³) and 200°C flue gas (about 0.75kg/m³), ΔP ≈ 9.81 × 5 × 0.54 ≈ 27Pa.
p-358.actionItem: If you use a stove today, inspect the flue joints and check your carbon monoxide alarm battery.

p-359.title: Laundry dries even while frozen in subzero weather
p-359.summary: Laundry hung out below freezing stiffens, yet it slowly dries by sublimation, with ice turning straight into vapor. No dryer is needed.
p-359.principle: Sublimation, H₂O(s) → H₂O(g), needs L_s ≈ 2.83kJ/g, and goes faster in dry, windy air.
p-359.example: Sublimating 1kg of water takes about 2.83MJ. It is slower than a dryer cycle (about 2-3kWh) but uses no electricity.
p-359.actionItem: On a clear, dry, subzero day today, hang a load outside and finish it indoors after shaking it out.

p-360.title: Clear snow off your car roof before driving
p-360.summary: Snow on a roof can fly off in chunks as you drive, hitting the car behind or blocking your windshield. Clear the roof, hood and glass before you leave.
p-360.principle: Wind from driving pushes snow chunks backward, and they strike the following car with kinetic energy E=12mv².
p-360.example: A 5cm layer of snow (assume 100kg/m³) on a 2m² roof weighs about 10kg. Hitting at a relative speed of 80km/h (22.2m/s) it carries about 2.5kJ.
p-360.actionItem: If it snowed today, brush all snow off the roof, hood and glass with a soft brush before driving.

p-361.title: Why you talk louder in a noisy restaurant
p-361.summary: As noise rises, people raise their voices without noticing, called the Lombard effect. When everyone does it, the room gets noisier still.
p-361.principle: In the Lombard effect, vocal level rises with noise to maintain the signal-to-noise ratio SNR=L_s-L_n needed to be heard.
p-361.example: When noise climbs 20dB, from 60 to 80dB, speech is known to rise by roughly 6-10dB. Restaurants can reach 70-80dB.
p-361.actionItem: At a gathering today, choose a corner seat away from speakers and lean toward the other person to talk more quietly.

p-362.title: The New Year sunrise comes earlier in the east
p-362.summary: The sun rises first in the east. At the same latitude, sunrise comes about 4 minutes earlier for every degree of longitude eastward.
p-362.principle: The Earth rotates 15^° per hour, so a 1^° longitude difference is 60 min15=4 min.
p-362.example: Homigot at 129.6°E is about 2.6° east of Seoul (127°E), so its sunrise is about 10 minutes earlier, with the actual gap differing slightly by latitude.
p-362.actionItem: If you plan to see the New Year sunrise, check the sunrise time for your destination in advance.

p-363.title: Tire pressure units bar, psi and kPa in one go
p-363.summary: Tire pressure is printed in bar, psi or kPa. Remember one conversion and you can switch any unit.
p-363.actionItem: Today, read the recommended pressure on the driver's door jamb and check your tires with a gauge.

p-364.title: Home EV charging time is kWh divided by kW
p-364.summary: Charging time is roughly the energy to add (kWh) divided by charger power (kW). Losses make it a bit longer in practice.
p-364.principle: t=(E / P), and with charging efficiency η, t=(E / η P).
p-364.example: Charging a 60kWh battery from 10% to 80% adds E=42kWh, and with a 7kW charger at 90% efficiency t=(42 / 0.9 × 7) ≈ 6.7 hours.
p-364.actionItem: Today, look up your car's battery capacity (kWh) and charger power (kW) and calculate the charging time.

p-365.title: Put a cup of water in first when melting snow for water
p-365.summary: Snow is full of air pockets and conducts heat poorly, so dropping it into an empty pot easily scorches the base. A little water first improves thermal contact and melts it much faster.
p-365.principle: Snow has low conductivity and large voids, so it contacts the pot over a small area. Melting needs latent heat of fusion L_f=334kJ/kg.
p-365.example: Making 1L of water takes about 334kJ, equal to heating water by 80°C. Snow is only about 10% water by volume, so you need about 10L of snow.
p-365.actionItem: If you melt snow for water today, warm a cup of water first and add clean snow gradually, and always boil before drinking.

p-366.title: Climb snowy hills with gentle acceleration and do not stop
p-366.summary: On a snowy uphill, a stop makes restarting hard and hard acceleration spins the wheels. Leave a gap before the hill and climb slowly at a steady pace.
p-366.principle: Static friction F ≤ µ_sN exceeds kinetic friction F=µ_kN (µ_s>µ_k), so grip drops sharply when the wheels spin.
p-366.example: On packed snow with µ ≈ 0.2, a 10% grade (θ ≈ 5.7^°) uses about 0.1mg for gravity out of about 0.2mg available friction, leaving only about 0.1mg spare.
p-366.actionItem: On a snowy hill today, leave a generous gap behind the car ahead and climb at a steady speed so you do not stop midway.
